{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZZZB2g", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhDAtS8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 73, "title": "Use period-oriented Japanese character weights for simulated terminal pacing", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `5ee5c56e51a48b624e94aa69dd84fe1a36d3dc85`, `src/output-renderer.ts` calculates display costs using `TextEncoder`, charging both `日` and half-width `ｶ` three UTF-8 bytes. `tests/progressive-output.spec.ts` explicitly requires these costs.

Consequently, Japanese menus, forum readings and other service output receive inappropriate relative pacing. At the existing nominal 300 mode, repeated Japanese characters and half-width kana both reveal at ten characters per second. A legacy-oriented approximation should distinguish fifteen common full-width Japanese characters from thirty half-width kana per second.

## Expected outcome

Replace UTF-8 display weights with a small, documented Shift-JIS-oriented approximation. Preserve the exact Unicode transcript and whole-grapheme reveal, existing nominal speed choices, queue safeguards and accessibility.

This changes perceived arrival timing only. It does not require a transcoder, codec dependency, storage migration or new terminal framework.

## Context

### Historical evidence and reconstruction decision

Sources were inspected live on 2026-10-23:

- [NEC PC-VAN office article, March 1993, printed page 230](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jkg/43/3/43_KJ00002959297/_pdf/-char/ja) explicitly lists Shift-JIS and NEC kanji communication conditions. The article also lists error-correction/compression support. Confidence is high for the documented earlier service configuration; continuity into November 1996 is a moderate-confidence reconstruction assumption. It does not establish measured display throughput.
- [WHATWG Shift_JIS encoder](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#shift_jis-encoder) supplies the technical single-byte versus double-byte distinction. This current standard explains encoding behavior; it is not historical PC-VAN evidence or a complete specification of NEC extensions.

Accept the following deliberately limited display-cost model: sum one unit for ASCII, half-width kana/punctuation U+FF61–U+FF9F, yen U+00A5 and overline U+203E; sum two units for every remaining code point. This covers the important common Japanese distinction without asserting exact Shift-JIS representability. The two-unit treatment of other Unicode, including emoji and combining marks, is an explicit modern fallback. Reveal complete graphemes after accumulating their full cost; never replace or normalize transcript text.

Retain one unit per LF and the existing nominal `bps / 10` unit budget. These remain reconstruction choices. Do not claim exact wire bytes, CRLF framing, compression, host delays or modem throughput.

### Implementation and history

- `src/output-renderer.ts` already separates logical text, grapheme costs and painted batches. Its pending-work bound uses string length independently of timing cost; preserve that separation.
- `tests/progressive-output.spec.ts` already drives controlled animation frames and verifies speed budgets, interleaved appends, queue overflow, reveal, announcements and preferences.
- `src/terminal.ts` preserves literal text, IME guards, command-triggered reveal and independent logical-log access.
- UTF-8 OSL preview sizes in `src/service-collections.ts` and UTF-8 forum identity hashing in `src/forums.ts` serve different purposes. Preserve them, along with UTF-8 log exports.
- [Issue #29](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/29) established approximate modem-era rendering and allowed an encoding-oriented cost model. This increment refines that completed scope. Live searches returned no open Issues or PRs; bounded history searches found no equivalent pending handoff.
- [PR #72](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/pull/72) matches the inspected baseline. Its description and `docs/validation.md` report 257 passing checks, including configured TypeScript checking and production build. Those are Coordinator records; this research graph ran no tests or builds. The review query returned no submissions, which does not establish absence of review elsewhere.

Scope is display weighting, focused regression coverage and explanatory documentation. Connection-stage delays, service commands, paging, content, scheduling and other service workflows remain separate.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement the documented weights without a full encoding table or new dependency. Representative costs include `A=1`, LF=1, `ｶ=1`, `日=2`, `あ=2`, `カ=2`, Japanese punctuation/full-width space=2, yen=1 and overline=1. Cover the half-width range boundaries. Empty input costs zero.
- [ ] Apply the explicit two-unit fallback per remaining code point, including supplementary characters and combining marks. Thus `😀=2`, `e\u0301=3` and `👩🏽‍💻=8`. Preserve their original text and reveal each grapheme atomically; these fallback costs are not authenticated historical transmission sizes.
- [ ] Retain nominal modes 300/1200/2400/9600 and Instant, defaults and saved preferences, reduced-motion behavior, asynchronous append order, batched painting, bounded pending work, skip, speed-change flushing and complete-batch announcements. Keep queue accounting independent of the new timing weights.
- [ ] Extend the existing controlled-frame coverage with fresh renderers showing that, after one second at nominal 300, ASCII and half-width kana each reveal 30 characters while repeated `日` reveals 15. Include a mixed-text boundary check demonstrating that a two-unit Japanese character waits for sufficient credit. Retain the existing ASCII budgets at every nominal speed and test combining/emoji integrity, complete logical output and queue draining. Update obsolete UTF-8 expectations without weakening ordering or batching assertions.
- [ ] Preserve literal whitespace/markup, IME and unsent drafts, command/reconnect behavior, scrolling, storage, consent, offline behavior and existing service journeys. UTF-8 logical-log downloads must still include accepted but unpainted output. Preserve actual UTF-8 OSL preview sizes and identity hashes; do not reuse display weights for those calculations.
- [ ] Update the pacing descriptions in README and `docs/terminal-display.md`, renderer comments and affected test wording. Add the historical evidence, inspected date, confidence, continuity assumption and fallback policy to `docs/research/pcvan-1996-1997.md` using its existing evidence conventions. Keep detailed provenance on demand and routine terminal output concise. Preserve earlier validation records as historical records; append actual new validation results.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs the documented `npm test` workflow before merge; its Playwright configuration includes TypeScript checking and production build. Preserve existing functional, storage, consent, IME and terminal regression coverage. Check changed documentation links, run `git diff --check`, review the final diff and report actual results or unresolved failures. No real inference or model download is needed.

## Optional validation

Further dated 1996 host/client documentation may refine encoding continuity or framing assumptions. Subjective pacing review, historical hardware and native IME observation are optional and are not completion gates.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. All acceptance checks are achievable before merge.
